question: Should OpenClaw adopt this two-layer exec denylist contract, including forced human approval for matches under `security=full` and `ask=off`?
rationale: The branch is technically coherent, but it adds persistent configuration and protocol surface and intentionally changes a high-impact command-authorization contract; maintainer security and product intent are required.

options.title: Adopt after integration
options.body: Accept both policy layers and deny-over-allow semantics after resolving current-main conflicts and adding exact-head hot-revocation proof.

options.title: Choose one policy owner
options.body: Keep the STOP-list behavior but expose it through only one canonical persisted configuration surface.

options.title: Decline deny-over-allow
options.body: Retain the existing deny, allowlist, and full modes without introducing a new exception policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt after integration
recommendation.body: Accept both policy layers and deny-over-allow semantics after resolving current-main conflicts and adding exact-head hot-revocation proof.
